participation.title: How to take part in building

rules.title: What you do is up to you
rules.desc: Unoccupied land in the server, or plots left open for new settlers, can be freely built on as long as they do not conflict with others' existing work. The server provides no official mainline projects or mandatory tasks; architecture, railways, machinery and all other projects are initiated and built by players themselves.

rules.title: Protect others' work
rules.desc: Free building rests on not infringing on others' existing work. Blocking others' roads, occupying reserved space, or damaging the integrity of existing builds without permission is strictly prohibited.

rules.title: Communicate first on public matters
rules.desc: Any modification or connection involving public facilities (main railways, public stations, main roads) or others' territory must be discussed with the relevant parties in advance, and only carried out once a consensus is reached.

rules.title: No unified building goal
rules.desc: HydCraft has no overall building blueprint enforced by the administration. How cities develop and how railways connect are entirely driven by spontaneous negotiation among players and progress step by step.

rules.title: Non-intervention unless necessary
rules.desc: The admin team follows a principle of non-intervention unless necessary, mainly handling operations and resolving conflicts. Admins only step in cases of malicious griefing, long-term land squatting, impacts on public areas, or irreconcilable disputes.

rules.title: Socializing is also part of building
rules.desc: HydCraft is essentially a community of acquaintances. All collaboration and planning are built on long-accumulated trust and mutual recognition among players. At its core, the point of playing is simply to have fun—and that remains our one guiding principle.

fitColumn.title: For people who like to build slowly
items: You enjoy long-term building and have a real interest in railways, cities, and architecture.
When roads, railways, terrain, or other people's plans are involved, you're willing to communicate in advance.
Being quiet is not a problem, as long as you're willing to explain your intent, respond when coordination is needed, and gradually build basic communication with the people around you.
You're comfortable with a server that has no fixed core gameplay loop, and you understand that much of the collaboration here is built on long-term trust among familiar players.
You respect other people's builds and don't damage or overwrite them at will.

unfitColumn.title: May not be a good fit if you want quick results
items: If what you're looking for is orderly construction, unified planning, or a stable place to prove your individual ability, this server may not be a good fit for you.
You don't want to communicate, but still want to reshape terrain, claim land, or force railway lines through.
You rely on strong in-game guidance and feel lost when no one tells you what to do next.
If you expect to arrive and immediately have a clear place, steady feedback, and ready-made collaborative relationships, this server may not be a good fit for you.
If you prefer to stay completely self-contained and don't want to respond to collaboration, communication, or relationship-building with others, you'll probably find it hard to fit in here.

baseline.title: Community Baseline
items: Follow the laws and regulations of mainland China. HydCraft has zero tolerance for illegal or non-compliant content.
The server is centered on building and collaboration. No real-world politics, no flame-baiting, and no factional hostility.
Do not form cliques to exclude others, and do not mock, attack, or damage other people's work. When disputes arise, contact the admin team for mediation first.

owner.roleLine: Server Owner, Chair of the Management Committee
owner.bioLine: I'm from Fuzhou, Fujian, a junior at a local non-elite university on a transfer-track path, and a TypeScript full-stack developer. The job market feels rough, even though I built basically the whole HydCraft website myself, haha. I'm not really a railway enthusiast or an architecture enthusiast. I just thought it seemed fun at first, and before I knew it, we had somehow kept this server going until now.

chiefArchitect.title: Chief Architects
chiefArchitect.subtitle: The core force behind the server's construction

cat.intro: From Shenzhen, Guangdong, and one of the map designers for Season 7 and Season 8. Excels at map drafting, small-scale design, and mechanical contraptions, with strong ideas and creativity in both architecture and structural mechanics. Handles European and American architectural styles especially well, particularly when weaving kinetic machinery into the overall design, and also enjoys musicals.

xw.intro: From Fuzhou, Fujian, and a close friend of catpillager. Specializes in small-scale European and American modern design, with standout work on both interiors and exteriors, especially in spatial detail, material texture, and atmosphere. He often collaborates with catpillager, forming a strong complement in architectural design and detail refinement.

fisheye.intro: From Shenyang, Liaoning, a Lindong City admin and the operator of Tongyun Railway. Known across the server for detailed structures and complete supporting works. Best at weaving clever machinery into a coherent system.

afe.motto: A city needs its outline first.
afe.intro: From Nanjing, Jiangsu, and a builder of Dongfeng in Season 6 and Edo in Season 7. Nina_Naganohara is good at organizing urban massing with clean block stacking, with Japanese style as the main axis and the occasional Chinese cadence. The work wins not by ornament, but by crisp silhouettes, clear district rhythm, and a steady skyline.

qishui.intro: From Guangzhou, Guangdong, a builder of Qinjing in Season 7, and afe's longtime partner. QiShui233 focuses on railways and stations, using refined material choices and unexpected station forms to make every stop worth a special visit.

qixuan.intro: From Langfang, Hebei, a builder of Guangyang in Seasons 5 and 7, a childhood friend of xxlm233, and a friend of Dotkk. qixuanjun233 likes hiding mechanical contraptions at street corners, shaping alleys with scenery that makes people slow down, and handling metro stations with a Beijing flavor.

xxlm.motto: Get the scale and detail right, and the atmosphere follows.
xxlm.intro: From Langfang, Hebei, a builder of Guangyang in Seasons 5 and 7, and qixuanjun233's childhood friend. xxlm233 favors the restraint, compactness, and precision of small-scale Japanese architecture, compressing the city into a light yet ordered scale. From vehicles and route organization to platform layouts, the work carries a strong JR feel.

dotkk.intro: From Shanghai, one of Guangyang's builders in Season 7, and a friend of qixuanjun233. Dotkk is the kind of builder who can raise a city's skeleton the moment he steps in, turning empty ground into urban order through road networks, building massing, and public space.

chuxia.intro: From Tianjin, one of the builders of Jiuxiang in Season 7, and a close teammate of ColaFrog and LanYue_CN. Chuxia_SF is especially strong with interiors, from furnishings and room flow to lived-in detail, and feels most at ease in places that demand patience, taste, and everyday texture.

items.question: Will the world save be released publicly?
items.answer: No full public release is planned. Players can take away the parts they built through blueprints, WorldEdit schematics, or similar export methods; when necessary, the admin team can also help with exports within a reasonable scope.

items.question: Why is there no official district map for Season 7?
items.answer: Because the actual building range, collaboration patterns, and practical boundaries of Season 7 have kept changing, there is still no district map that would stay accurate for long. Rather than publishing a map that goes stale quickly, we prefer to coordinate case by case around districts, roads, railways, and public facilities during real construction.

items.question: Is QQ still the only main entry point right now?
items.answer: Yes. The QQ group is still the main communication entry. Most members are mainland China players, so routine notices, client downloads, reviews, and construction coordination are all mostly handled there.

items.question: Can a newcomer start building right away?
items.answer: Yes, but it's better to first look around at the existing roads, railways, public facilities, and nearby builds. Ordinary personal buildings usually do not require complicated approval; if it involves city districts, railway access, large public works, or possible impact on other people's areas, talk first.

items.question: Does the server enforce a unified building style?
items.answer: No strict unified style is enforced. HydCraft cares more about the urban relationships that form naturally over long-term building, and whether players can collaborate steadily; as long as a build does not clearly damage the public environment, maliciously occupy land, or interfere with others, style differences are usually not something we step in over.

items.question: What if I only want to visit and look around?
items.answer: That's fine. You can join the group first, learn the basics, then enter the server after downloading the client. If you're only visiting for a short time, you do not need to jump into large-scale building right away.

items.question: Can I bring friends with me?
items.answer: Yes, absolutely. Friends and classmates are welcome. We just ask them to join through the normal entry path and read the rules first.

items.question: Can I still join if I'm not good at building?
items.answer: Absolutely. Building skill has never been the barrier here. If there's open space and your plan does not step on someone else's layout, you can just start building. Whether it looks impressive comes second. We care much more about social connection and collaboration, and the overall atmosphere matters far more than individual technique. Even though the server does have a Ranking system, it is only meant as encouragement, not as a way to sort people into tiers by building level.
